text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated 5xx rate across prod-gateway in eu-west-1 (threshold breach). spike started ~10:45 UTC. paging jen (oncall).
jen: I’m on it. Can someone post customer impact ETA? seeing ~15% error-rate for /v1/generate on some routes.
luis: grabbing logs now. any change pushed in last 30m? I see no deploys from deploy-bot in that window.
maya: checking edge proxy pools and cert rotator health. nothing obvious in autoscaler.
emily: support seeing ~40 open tickets for timeouts, some customers report session failures. escalating to sasha.
sasha: notifying affected accounts with temp mitigation steps, asking for workarounds.
jen: ok priority: confirm root cause (config vs cert), mitigate (route traffic/fallback), communicate. luis, can you tail the gateway TLS handshake errors?
luis: past 10m from gw logs:

```
2026-03-15T10:46:12Z gateway[proxy-12] handshake_error: tlsv1_alert_unknown_ca: client hello failed
2026-03-15T10:46:13Z gateway[proxy-09] handshake_error: certificate_expired: peer_cert expired
2026-03-15T10:46:14Z gateway[proxy-11] tls_alert: unknown_ca during mTLS verification
```

luis: seems like a CA chain / intermediate issue; some proxies report expired intermediate. not all proxies hit.
carol: side question: any recent CA rotations or KMS changes? security rotations were scheduled earlier today for internal mTLS anchor but I thought they were staged for next week.
maya: rotator logs show a failed upload to the edge config store at 10:44 UTC (permission denied). suspect partial rollout.
frank: that lines up with routing anomalies — some edge nodes got new chain, others still serving old chain => mismatch causing handshake rejects.
jen: high-level action: 1) pause any further rotator runs, 2) pin traffic away from affected nodes, 3) restore previous cert chain to nodes that received bad upload.
ryan: can we quick-fail to a compatible model or route to dedicated tier to reduce customer impact while we fix TLS? we can route non-sensitive traffic to dedicated in another region.
jen: yes, set fallback routes. maya, can you start traffic steering via lb rules to eu-north and usa regions for non-EU customers?
maya: starting traffic steer. `kubectl patch svc/gateway -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"traffic-override":"steer-eu-north"}}}'` — applying now.
maya: steer applied to 37% of traffic in 30s, monitoring.
emily: CS reported a big customer (AcmeCo) with API timeouts; they've been notified and given a temporary region switch. they're asking for ETA.
sasha: AcmeCo notified, they can switch region; they're asking for an ETA on full restoration.
jen: ETA depends on rollbacks. luis, can you roll back the cert upload on proxies that got the bad chain?
luis: yes — I can push the previous chain to affected hosts. will run cert-rollback script:

```
for host in $(list-proxy-nodes --filter affected); do scp old_chain.pem $host:/etc/edge/chain.pem && ssh $host 'systemctl restart edge-proxy'; done
```

luis: kicking off, ETA ~12m for batch.
frank: note — after restart there might be a brief spike in 502s as backend connections re-establish. plan accordingly.
jen: good call. notify support and CS so they can set expectations.
emily: posted message to affected customers: "we're implementing a fix; expected restoration within 20 minutes. intermittent 5xx may occur during rollback." acked by AcmeCo.
deploy-bot: deployment notice: "cert-rotator job detected failure at 10:44 UTC; halted further runs." (automated)
luis: rollback batch 1 done — 9 hosts updated, checks show handshake success on those nodes now. error rate dropped from 15% to 7%.
maya: LB health shows traffic shifting away from remaining flaky nodes, targeted draining in progress.
carol: I'm pulling rotator IAM policies. looks like token used by rotator was rotated without updating service account binding — upload failed with 403.
frank: so root cause: token rotation caused partial failure of cert rotator job, leading to inconsistent chain distribution. need postmortem and a safer rollout strategy.
jen: agreed. immediate priority is full restoration. luis/maya continue rollback until error-rate back to baseline <1%.
ryan: added temporary gateway fallback: prioritizing TLS-compatible nodes and enabling permissive TLS for legacy clients for 10 minutes (will log only). this should reduce failures for older clients.
luis: batch 2 done, batch 3 in progress. currently 3 nodes remain with bad chain.
emily: tickets note updated; churn expected during restarts.
sasha: ACMECo confirmed partial recovery after switching region; wants post-incident summary.
jen: once all nodes rolled back, we'll re-run rotator in dry-run mode with explicit service-account check. carol, can you update rotation runbook to require token verification preflight?
carol: yes I'll add preflight checks and a kill-switch. also adding alerting rule for partial-rotation inconsistencies.
maya: last 3 hosts rolled back at 10:58 UTC — running full health check.
luis: healthchecks green across all proxies; 5xx back down to 0.8% at 11:00 UTC.
jen: good. marking incident as mitigated. remaining work: root-cause writeup, runbook updates, customer comms, and retro.
emily: sending final note to impacted customers with apology and mitigation steps. will include temporary credits.
sasha: collecting affected account list and impact windows.
frank: follow-ups for ops: add stronger atomicity to rotator, verify IAM rotation choreography, and add canary rollout with verification at each stage.
jen: oncall handoff to luis for final checks and writeup. luis — you own the incident page and timeline?
luis: taking it. I'll post timeline, logs, and remediation steps in the incident tracker within 2 hours.
jen: thanks everyone. incident-bot, please log severity=P2, created=2350001234, mitigated=2350001540, summary="Partial cert-rotator failure caused inconsistent CA chain on subset of edge proxies, triggering TLS handshake failures and elevated 5xx. Rolled back chain, traffic steering, and fallback enabled." 
incident-bot: Logged incident P2. Follow-up tasks assigned: rotator-runbook, IAM preflight, canary verification.
ryan: small note — we should add a metric for 'cert-chain-divergence' to catch this earlier.
carol: agreed. adding to security backlog.
emily: closing customer comms after approval from jen.
jen: closing thread once luis posts the incident doc. thanks all for quick response. :white_check_mark:"
